summary: mountainash-rules gives you a concise, expressive way to define business rules as tabular data and evaluate them in a single vectorized pass. Define your dimensions, choose from 11 match strategies, load your rules, and get ranked results with full per-dimension explainability. For combinatorial problems, the AccumulatorEngine builds a compact lattice of valid rule combinations with provenance tracking.
use_cases: Pricing engine: evaluate a customer context against hundreds of pricing rules and retrieve the best-matching tier with a full explanation of why it won.
Eligibility screening: define eligibility criteria across multiple dimensions and instantly see which rules a given applicant satisfies.
Configuration selection: match device or environment attributes to configuration profiles, ranked by specificity.
Portfolio allocation: use the AccumulatorEngine to find all valid combinations of investment rules for a given risk profile, with accumulated totals.

concepts.name: Defining dimensions
concepts.description: Dimensions describe the axes your rules operate on. Each dimension pairs a data column with a MatchStrategy (EXACT, RANGE, REGEX, SET_MEMBERSHIP, and more), giving you fine-grained control over how context values are compared to rule metadata.

concepts.name: Single-context rule evaluation
concepts.description: Pass a context dictionary to ExpressionRulesEngine.evaluate() and receive a RuleResult containing every surviving rule, ranked by specificity. Access the best match, count survivors, or iterate the full ranked list.

concepts.name: Explainability
concepts.description: Every evaluation result carries a per-dimension ternary breakdown (match / unknown / non-match) so you can see exactly which dimensions contributed to a rule's survival and which were neutral. Call explain() on any rule to get the full picture.

concepts.name: Accumulator: building and applying rule lattices
concepts.description: The AccumulatorEngine handles problems where you need valid combinations of rules rather than a single winner. Build a Lattice from your rule set, then apply a context to retrieve accumulated values (sums, counts) with full provenance showing which rules contributed to each combination.

concepts.name: Partitioned lattices (CONTEXT_KEY dimensions)
concepts.description: Mark dimensions as CONTEXT_KEY to partition your rule set before building lattices. The engine builds a separate lattice per partition and apply_auto() selects the correct one at evaluation time, keeping large rule sets fast and memory-efficient.
